correctness.rationale: For each pair the dot product is uniform on [-1,1], so Z and 1/Z have the same survival 1/(1+z^2) and mean π/2. On Z≥1 the reciprocating term is bounded and the rescaled density converges to 2r^-3 along the collision ray; on Z<1 exchange Z and 1/Z to get the antipodal ray (zero if the parameter vector vanishes). Distinct pair kernels are independent in pairs, including edges sharing one point by conditioning on that point and rotational invariance. With finitely many edges, two contributions above a fixed fraction of x have probability O(x^-4). For a test function supported away from zero, a nonzero test contribution forces some edge to exceed a fixed positive fraction of x; a uniform continuity bound on the event only that edge exceeds a much smaller fraction proves additivity as the latter fraction tends to zero. Multiplication by 2/n yields binom(n,2)(2/n)^2=c_n; the deterministic centering is irrelevant to the limit. For unbounded tail sets, the union bound gives uniform x^2-scaled mass O(M^-2) outside radius M, so vague convergence can be applied to the two scalar tails with boundary of measure zero. This yields c_n(1+a_+^2) and c_n a_-^2; integration and inversion then give the moment threshold, 2c_n(1+a^2) log x, and upper quantile constant. Covers n=2, negative and zero a, and coincident or absent rays. The supplied numerical checker was read, not run; its finite scalar checks do not certify the finite-sum theorem.
residual_risks: No simultaneous growing-n limit, error bound for a fixed significance level, or formal verification is inferred.
